objectives.text: Determine the status of the 27 registered personnel
Establish the cause and sequence of the vessel's failures
Determine whether the vessel presents a continuing hazard

inspect_lifeboats.label: Inspect lifeboat systems and launch telemetry
inspect_lifeboats.log: Lifeboat manifest and launch telemetry recovered.

E-01.name: Reactor SCRAM Record
E-01.finding:
Chief Engineer Tomas Varga manually initiated the reactor shutdown after Impact Event 01.

The record establishes that the reactor shutdown was deliberate, but does not by itself establish whether it was appropriate.

E-02.name: Heat-Rejection System Failure Analysis
E-02.finding:
Impact Event 01 damaged external coolant manifolds and multiple radiator sections.

The protected internal primary coolant circuit remained intact.

Remaining external heat-rejection capacity was insufficient for safe sustained reactor operation.

Safe reactor restart was not possible.

E-03.name: Environmental Impact and Navigation Record
E-03.finding:
Impact Event 01 occurred while the crew was aboard and damaged primary communications and the external heat-rejection system.

Before evacuation, Navigation identified a second high-density debris concentration. Petrel's ballistic trajectory would intersect it approximately nine hours after Impact Event 01.

Petrel could not maneuver clear. The lifeboats could.

Impact Event 02 occurred after the crew evacuated and breached the Aft Survey Bay.

This evidence establishes cause, chronology, and the rationale behind evacuation.

E-06.name: Lifeboat Manifest and Launch Telemetry
E-06.finding:
27 personnel were verified aboard three lifeboats.

Lifeboat 01: 9
Lifeboat 02: 9
Lifeboat 03: 9

All three successfully separated from Petrel. Initial course changes were confirmed.

This establishes that all registered personnel left Petrel alive. It does NOT establish their later fate.
